summary: Firelookout.ca lists a steel Palmerston Fire Tower with a Tweed, Ontario address, placed on a 1977 Pembroke topographic map; no current source describes it.

facts.status_note: Only one source describes it, a firelookout.ca directory entry; no source describes the site today.

evidence.supports: structure is steel and appears on a 1977 Pembroke topographic map sheet 31F
evidence.quote: Steel. Appears on Pembroke topographic map 31F, 3rd ed., 1977

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Prevention Act of 1917 set Ontario's fire protection procedures
evidence.quote: of 1917 determined fire protection procedures for Ontario

evidence.supports: the Act divided the province into districts, each under a District Forester
evidence.quote: The Act divided the province into separate districts, each under the complete authority of a District Forester.

evidence.supports: towers were judged the best general method of fire detection where communication was reliable
evidence.quote: Towers were considered to be the best means of general detection in areas where good communication could be provided.

evidence.supports: observer learned the surrounding land and could see smoke or fire right away
evidence.quote: The observer, looking out for his tower, became familiar with the area and was able to note any smoke or fires as soon as they occurred.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one firelookout.ca entry with no build year, height, type or status, plus a general Ontario background marker. The pin (45.00139, -76.83722) is not one of the firelookout.ca Tweed town-centre placeholder pins (44.47473, -77.31025) but is well north of Tweed, so the address may be a loose reference. No LIO fire-tower record and no entry on the volunteer still-standing list was found for Palmerston. A Wikipedia article on Tweed says the Tweed Forest Fire District was founded in 1922 and ran 21 lookout towers, but no source found ties Palmerston to that district, so the story does not say so. The 1977 Pembroke sheet 31F is a Crown topographic map that could place the tower; it was not checked. The marker is general background, not about this tower.
